name: Managed authentication and protected workspace
covers: auth session restoration before protected data
description: Verifies real provider-managed authentication gates TextGuard and the authenticated user can reach the existing workspace.
steps: Open TextGuard in a signed-out browser session
Verify the branded sign-in screen appears before workspace content
Continue to the AppDeploy managed sign-in screen and complete an enabled provider flow
Verify the authenticated user returns to the TextGuard workspace after session restoration
Sign out from Account Profile and verify the login screen is shown
expected: The provider authenticates the user, the SDK restores the identity on app startup, protected API routes reject missing/invalid credentials, and logout clears the session.

name: User-scoped profile persistence and isolation
covers: profile data isolation by authenticated user ID
description: Confirms profile records are persisted in the AppDeploy database using the authenticated user ID as the record key.
steps: Sign in with test account A and open Account Profile
Save a changed display name and reload the page
Verify the saved name and first-seen date remain
Sign out and sign in with test account B
Verify account B cannot read or change account A's profile
expected: Each profile endpoint requires a valid AppDeploy token and reads/writes only the record keyed by ctx.user.userId. No password fields or password hashes are stored by TextGuard.

name: Preserve comparison workflows after authentication
covers: hash table Trie token arrays and Rabin-Karp visualizations
description: Checks that the existing algorithm and document comparison modules remain available after the new authentication gate.
steps: Sign in and upload two deterministic TXT documents with a shared five-word phrase
Run Similarity Checker and open the comparison report
Inspect both original-offset highlights
Open Algorithm Analysis and visit all four sections
Open Detection History and export CSV and print report
expected: The original client-side DSA engine, document selection, comparisons, highlights, visualizations and reports remain functional after sign-in. Existing history remains session-only.

name: Responsive authentication and profile pages
description: Checks the authentication entry screen and profile view on narrow mobile and desktop widths.
steps: Open the signed-out login page at 375x667
Verify the sign-in and create-account actions fit the viewport
Complete provider sign-in and open Account Profile
Verify profile fields and sign-out remain usable at 375x667
Resize to 1280x800 and verify the full layout
expected: Login, provider redirect, profile editing and logout controls remain visible and operable on mobile and desktop without unintended horizontal overflow.

name: Comparison results restore across navigation and refresh
covers: Comparison Results available after sidebar navigation
sessionStorage restoration of documents and comparison runs
description: Verifies completed engine results are retained for the browser tab and the selected comparison remains available after navigation or reload.
steps: Sign in and upload two deterministic TXT documents
Run a comparison and verify its report is added to Detection History
Navigate directly to Comparison Results from the sidebar and verify the completed pair is displayed
Navigate to another section and return to Comparison Results
Refresh the browser and reopen Comparison Results
Open the corresponding Detection History report
Run a second comparison and verify the latest result is selected
Attempt to open an unavailable comparison identifier and verify a clear empty/error state
expected: The latest completed comparison is displayed consistently after section navigation and reload; session document snapshots and history restore from sessionStorage; historical reports show their selected data; unavailable IDs never fall back to stale or fabricated results.
